title: How is a file made?
question: open() with O_CREAT makes a file that is not there. What does the kernel make? (In memory: ramfs.)
text: open() with O_CREAT makes a file that is not there. What does the kernel make?

The path walk reaches "new.txt" and finds no such name; with O_CREAT, [lookup_open](1:lookup_open) asks the file system to make it. In ramfs, [ramfs_mknod](1:ramfs_mknod) makes two things: a new inode, which is the file itself (its mode, its size, its pages), and a name for it in the directory, a dentry pointing at that inode.
Then the open goes on as any open: a `struct file`, a slot in the fd table, and the call returns the fd.
Try: create the same file twice (add the first call again): the second time the name is there, so `lookup_open` takes the other branch. Add `O_EXCL` to the second one and it fails with EEXIST.
